notes: Account summary: building a latency-first personalization layer for a live commerce product. Very cost-sensitive at scale — margins tighten above 2M monthly requests.
Workload characteristics: large number of short-turn interactions (10-80 tokens), high concurrency during peak drops (up to 1.5k qps), strict p95 latency SLOs (target: <80ms for 64-token responses).

Tech preferences: open to LlamaX-family and Mistral variants if quantized. Currently testing int8/4-bit quantized weights in-house; wants Redwood Optimize suggestions for quant profile that balances quality and cost.

Batching/caching interest: wants automatic batching up to 8-16 while preserving tail latency. Very interested in prefix/KV cache for repeat prompts (session personalization). Asked for guidance on cache TTLs and cache-hit instrumentation.

Perf benchmarking ask: Redwood to supply end-to-end p50/p95/p99, token/sec, GPU utilization, and cost-per-1M tokens for (a) baseline unquantized, (b) int8 quant, (c) int4 quant with pruning. Include comparison vs Triton + DeepSpeed baseline (they will provide traces).
Routing/fallback needs: multi-region routing (US East primary, EU failover), fallback to lower-cost quantized model on high load, must support consistent API surface for canary rollouts.

Security/compliance: requires SSO (SAML), KMS integrations for key wrapping, audit logs retained 1 year. Legal flagged data residency clause for EU customers — may need Private deployment in EU region.

POC plan: 2-week benchmark with synthetic and sampled production traffic. Week 1: baseline runs and tuning (batch sizes, cache policies). Week 2: prolonged soak with failover and routing tests. Success metrics: p95 under SLO, quality regression <2% on eval set, 30-40% token-cost reduction vs baseline.
Quotes / paraphrases: 'Latency is our product — if inference adds jitter we lose conversions.' — Head of Product.
Commercial: prefers committed Dedicated capacity if POC shows stable p95 and unit-cost savings. Wants options for reserved burst capacity and SLA language for enterprise contract.
